players.product: custom SoC / AI ASIC design platform and turnkey ASIC services (Samsung Foundry DSP; GlobalFoundries platinum partner)

quarterly_data.signal: IR deck (1Q26 earnings release, consolidated): 1Q26 new orders KRW 55.4bn (+17.1% YoY, +25.6% QoQ), with mass-production orders of KRW 15.7bn in the quarter (1Q25 KRW 8.0bn, 4Q25 KRW 5.6bn) as 'the full-scale expansion of mass-production orders begins'. Annual new orders have risen from KRW 5.7bn in 2020 to KRW 123.9bn in 2024 and KRW 168.4bn in 2025. The company says overseas orders surged from 2025 and it expects global sales growth to continue, centred on North America and Japan.
quarterly_data.figure: 1Q26 new orders KRW 55.4bn (+17.1% YoY); mass-production orders KRW 15.7bn; FY2025 new orders KRW 168.4bn

quarterly_data.signal: Business mix per the deck: 1Q26 revenue rose 137.1% YoY and 54.0% QoQ, split into IP business KRW 16.3bn and ASIC development KRW 28.0bn, with the remainder from mass production. FY2025 revenue KRW 121.0bn: ASIC development KRW 70.9bn, IP KRW 30.5bn and mass production KRW 19.6bn (more than 2x YoY as products whose development began in the company's early years entered full mass production from 2H25). Management commentary: the IP business is shifting to high-margin off-the-shelf and leading-edge (2/3nm) IP, with analog IP demand rising as thermal and power management gain importance in datacenter AI ASICs; the ASIC development portfolio pairs high-value 2/4nm datacenter AI ASICs with 5/8nm edge and device AI ASICs. The deck cites the global AI ASIC market growing to over US$300 billion by 2029.
quarterly_data.figure: 1Q26 revenue +137.1% YoY; IP KRW 16.3bn / ASIC development KRW 28.0bn; FY2025 mass production KRW 19.6bn (2x+ YoY)

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 mass-production schedule shown in the deck (customers in Korea, Japan, China and India): 5nm datacenter AI inference chip, 5nm NPU chip, 14nm edge AI inference chip, 8nm CCTV AI inference chip, 14nm memory controller chip, and 22nm+ mobile touch-driver, mobile display-driver, MCU and interposer products; the company says mass-production growth that began in 2H25 continued in 1Q26 and the follow-on pipeline is expanding as planned. Turnkey track record includes 500mm2 (4nm) and 500/800mm2 (8nm) big-die projects, with a project for an Asian HPC AI chip company ('P') in progress. Platform case study: a 14nm AI accelerator took 148 man-months and 10 months vs 605 man-months and 23 months the traditional way (75% and 56% less).
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 ramps: 5nm datacenter AI inference, 5nm NPU, 14nm edge AI inference, 8nm CCTV AI chips; big-die 500/800mm2 (8nm)
